title: Character cottages listed below £364,270 average price
summary:
Nine character cottages across Scotland, England and Wales have been listed below the current national average asking price of £364,270, according to the House Price Index for November 2026. The properties feature traditional cottage characteristics including exposed beams, wood-burning stoves and period features, with prices ranging from £225,000 to £350,000.

title: Hammersmith office building approved for 139-home conversion
summary:
A four-storey office building in Hammersmith has received prior approval from the London Borough of Hammersmith & Fulham to be converted into 139 rental homes. Griffin House, located at 161 Hammersmith Road, will comprise 131 one-person homes and eight two-person homes, with completion targeted within 12 months.

title: Land Registry urges agents to use local charges search
summary:
HM Land Registry is encouraging estate agents to utilise its local land charges search service before listing properties, warning that failure to identify restrictions early could impact transaction timelines. The service provides instant results for £15, though coverage remains incomplete across England and Wales.

title: Free damp and mould recording tool launched for landlords
summary:
A property maintenance company has launched a free digital tool allowing landlords and letting agents to create dated records of damp and mould conditions in rental properties. Room by Room enables users to conduct property inspections using a mobile phone, producing PDF reports with photographs and timestamps.

title: Estate agency software adds AI automation for follow-ups
summary:
Agency Office has released an updated CRM system that uses AI and automated workflows to handle routine follow-up tasks for residential estate agents. The platform consolidates communications and generates response suggestions requiring human approval before sending.

summary:

title: Landlords seek data protection clarity on rental register
summary:
The National Residential Landlords Association has requested intervention from the Information Commissioner's Office regarding data protection on the Government's new private rented sector database. The landlord database is scheduled to begin its phased rollout across England on 15th December.

title: Government plans to collect interest from tenancy deposits
summary:
The Department for Housing, Communities and Local Government is proposing legislation to collect a portion of interest earned from tenants' deposits held in custodial schemes. The changes could take effect from March 2027, affecting deposits worth billions of pounds in England.

The post Government plans to collect interest from tenancy deposits appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Scotland reduces EPC validity period to five years from 2028
summary:
Energy Performance Certificates in Scotland will be valid for five years instead of 10 under new regulations passed by the Scottish Government. The change takes effect on 30th April 2028 as part of Scotland's wider EPC reforms, creating a divergence with England and Wales where certificates remain valid for 10 years.
